@@ -1,72 +1,166 @@
-**MetaDescription**: Create and manage custom agents in VS Code for specialized development roles, tools, and workflows.
+**MetaDescription**: Reuse, create, and manage custom agents in VS Code for specialized development roles and workflows.
 
 # Custom agents in VS Code
 
 Custom agents combine instructions, tools, and an optional language model into a reusable configuration for a specific role, such as planning or code review. Switch to a custom agent instead of repeating the same instructions and selecting tools for every conversation.
 
-This article shows you how to create, use, and manage custom agents in VS Code, configure their files, and connect them with handoffs.
+Start with one recurring task where the default agent needs more specific guidance. This article walks through creating a code review agent, checking its results, and refining it before sharing it with your team. For file locations, syntax, and harness-specific options, see the [Custom agent file reference](/docs/agents/reference/custom-agent-file-reference.md).
+
+## When to use a custom agent
+
+Create a custom agent when a recurring role needs its own instructions, tools, or output format. For example:
+
+* Review code against your team's criteria with reading and search tools.
+* Investigate how a feature works and return findings with file references.
+* Produce implementation plans that follow your team's required structure.
+
+You don't need a custom agent for every task. Use the [built-in planning workflow](/docs/agents/run/planning.md) if it already meets your needs. Put project-wide conventions in [custom instructions](/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions.md), and put one-time requirements in your prompt. For reusable workflows with supporting scripts or resources, consider an [agent skill](/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills.md).
+
+See the [customization comparison](/docs/agents/concepts/customization.md#customization-options-at-a-glance) if you're unsure which option fits.
+
+## Reuse an agent from a plugin
+
+Before creating a custom agent, [browse customization marketplaces](/docs/agent-customization/overview.md#discover-and-install-existing-customizations-preview) for a plugin that includes the role you need.
+
+1. Select a plugin and review its included agents, instructions, tools, and setup requirements. Confirm that it supports your intended harness.
+1. [Install the plugin](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md#install-a-plugin-from-a-marketplace) and complete its setup.
+1. [Select the agent in chat](#use-a-custom-agent) if it supports user invocation, or use it as a [subagent](/docs/agents/run/subagents.md#run-a-custom-agent-as-a-subagent) as intended by the publisher.
+1. Try a representative task and review the agent's response and tool calls before relying on it.
+
+Manage the installation through the [Plugins section](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md#view-installed-plugins). Create your own agent when you need a role or configuration that the available plugins don't provide.
+
+## Create a custom agent
 
 > [!TIP]
-> **Not sure which customization to use?** See the [decision matrix](/docs/agents/concepts/customization.md#customization-options-at-a-glance) to compare custom agents with prompt files, agent skills, and the other options.
-
-## When to use a custom agent
-
-Create a custom agent when a recurring task needs its own instructions, tools, or model. For example:
-
-* Restrict a code review agent to read-only tools and give it your team's review criteria.
-* Give a planning agent your team's plan template and hand off to an implementation agent.
-* Run a focused research agent as a [subagent](/docs/agents/run/subagents.md#run-a-custom-agent-as-a-subagent) to keep its work out of the main conversation's context.
-* Share the same workflow with your repository or organization.
-
-Custom agents appear in the agent picker alongside the [built-in agents](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#choose-a-built-in-agent). The tools and controls available to a custom agent depend on the selected [agent harness](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md).
-
-When you select a custom agent, it applies to your requests until you switch agents. In the Copilot harness, the agent's instructions are added to your [custom instructions](/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions.md) and take precedence if they conflict. If the agent specifies a `tools` list, only those tools are available. Another agent can also run a custom agent as a subagent, or a [handoff](#handoffs) can switch the conversation to it.
-
-## Create a custom agent
-
-Use the [Agent Customizations editor](/docs/agent-customization/overview.md#agent-customizations-editor) to create an agent in your workspace or at the user level.
-
-Use the **Session Target** UI control to [select the agent harness](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#select-a-harness) you intend to use, then open the editor from either surface:
-
-* **Agents window**: Select **Customizations** in the left sidebar to open the Agent Customizations editor. Then select **Agents**.
-
-* **Chat view**: Select **Open Customizations** in the Chat view title bar, or run **Chat: Open Customizations** from the Command Palette (``Shortcut: workbench.action.showCommands``). Then select **Agents**.
-
-The editor shows customizations for the selected harness. Follow these steps to create an agent file:
-
-1. Select **New Agent** (plus icon) next to the **Workspace** or **User** group, depending on where you want to store the agent file.
+> Before creating an agent, check whether a plugin already provides one for your task. [Browse and install plugins from a marketplace](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md#install-a-plugin-from-a-marketplace). Review the plugin's included agents and harness compatibility before installing it.
+
+The following steps use the **Copilot** harness and create a workspace agent that you can share through source control. Other harnesses have different file formats and tool rules. See [harness compatibility](/docs/agents/reference/custom-agent-file-reference.md#harness-compatibility) before reusing the file with another harness.
+
+1. Open your project folder and select the **Copilot** harness in chat.
+
+1. Run **Chat: Open Customizations** from the Command Palette (``Shortcut: workbench.action.showCommands``) to open the [Agent Customizations editor](/docs/agent-customization/overview.md#agent-customizations-editor) and then select the **Agents** tab.
+
+1. Select **New Agent** (plus icon) next to **Workspace**.
 
     ![Screenshot showing the Agent Customizations editor and the dropdown to create a new custom agent.](images/customization/create-custom-agent-2.png)
 
-    Alternatively, run the **Chat: New Custom Agent** command from the Command Palette (``Shortcut: workbench.action.showCommands``).
-
-1. Select the location and enter a file name for the custom agent. This is the default name that appears in the agents dropdown.
-
-1. Provide the details in the newly created `.agent.md` file, and then save it.
-
-    * Fill in the YAML frontmatter to configure the agent's name, description, tools, and other options.
-    * Add instructions for the agent in the body of the file. Use the [planning agent example](#custom-agent-file-structure) as a starting point.
-
-1. [Select your custom agent in chat](#use-a-custom-agent) and try a prompt to check that it follows your instructions.
-
-You can modify existing custom agents by opening them in the Agent Customizations editor.
-
-> [!TIP]
-> You can let an agent generate a custom agent for you based on a description. For example, enter a prompt like "Create a workspace custom agent for code reviews."
-
-### Custom agent file structure
-
-A custom agent file combines an optional FrontMatter header with Markdown instructions. The header configures the agent's name, description, tools, and other options. The Markdown body describes what the agent should do and what it should return.
-
-For all supported fields and defaults, see the [Custom agent file reference](/docs/agents/reference/custom-agent-file-reference.md).
-
-For example, save this planning agent as `.github/agents/planner.agent.md`. It uses read-only tools to research a task and return a plan:
+1. Choose the workspace location and enter `reviewer` as the file name.
+
+1. Replace the generated file contents with the following example. Adapt the review criteria to problems your team repeatedly encounters.
+
+    ```markdown
+    ---
+    name: Reviewer
+    description: Review code for incorrect behavior and missing tests without editing files
+    tools: ['read', 'search']
+    ---
+    Review the code supplied in the request. Read related code and tests
+    when needed to check the behavior.
+
+    Focus on:
+    * Incorrect behavior and unhandled errors.
+    * Missing tests for important behavior and error cases.
+
+    Report only actionable findings. For each finding, include the file
```

 * **Matcher behavior:** Local ignores matcher values. Copilot applies documented matcher rules, including different semantics for compatible `PreToolUse` names. Recheck every filter, including invalid patterns and tools it should not match.
 * **SDK callback types:** programmatic callbacks are not JSON-file command hooks. A field in SDK source, such as a callback-only prompt override, is not evidence that a shell hook can use it.

 ## How customization changes an agent
 
-Without customization, the agent works from your prompt, the current conversation, and the context it gathers from your workspace. Customizations add information or capabilities that persist beyond a single prompt. They can change different parts of the agent's work:
+The model brings general knowledge learned during training. The agent combines that knowledge with your prompt, the current conversation, and available context, such as workspace files. Your organization's internal practices and information in other projects aren't automatically available. Customizations provide reusable guidance and access to additional capabilities, so you don't have to supply the same context in every prompt.
 
-* **Provide context**: [instructions](/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions.md) describe coding standards, architecture decisions, and other rules the agent should follow.
-* **Define repeatable work**: [agent skills](/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills.md) and [prompt files](/docs/agent-customization/prompt-files.md) package task-specific guidance so you don't have to describe the same process in every conversation.
-* **Configure a role**: [custom agents](/docs/agent-customization/custom-agents.md) combine instructions, tools, and a language model into a specialized agent persona.
-* **Add capabilities**: [MCP servers](/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers.md) give the agent tools for interacting with external systems such as databases, browsers, and APIs.
-* **Automate lifecycle actions**: [hooks](/docs/agent-customization/hooks.md) run commands at specific points in the agent loop, independent of whether the model chooses to run them.
-* **Adopt a ready-made setup**: [agent plugins](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md) let you install multiple related customization types as one package.
+Different mechanisms change different parts of the agent's work. Instructions and workflows guide the model's decisions. Tools expand the actions it can take. Hooks run commands at specific points in the agent's workflow, such as before or after a tool runs, without relying on the model to request them. Plugins package related customizations for installation and sharing.
 
-For supported services, [Copilot connectors](/docs/agent-customization/copilot-connectors.md) `feature(copilot-connectors)` provide a managed alternative to configuring an MCP server. Connectors add MCP tools to Copilot harness sessions without installing a local server or writing configuration.
-
-These mechanisms affect different layers of the agent. Instructions guide the model's decisions, tools expand the actions it can take, and hooks run outside the model's decision-making. Adding a rule to an instructions file is not equivalent to executing a validation script. Neither mechanism alone establishes a security boundary.
+Adding a rule to an instructions file is not equivalent to executing a validation script. Neither mechanism alone establishes a security boundary.
 
 Relevant customizations can reduce back-and-forth and rework by giving the agent project context from the start. Avoiding corrective turns and discarded implementations can help reduce [AI credit usage](/docs/agents/guides/optimize-usage.md). Keep customizations focused because their content also consumes space in the model's context window.
 
 ## Customization options at a glance
 
-Start from an observed problem instead of adding customization by default. Define a representative task and its expected outcome. If the result already meets your needs, stop. Otherwise, try the smallest change that addresses the repeated problem.
-
-Before creating files, [check the selected harness and supported locations](/docs/agent-customization/overview.md#check-harness-compatibility). Choosing a language model doesn't change the customization formats that a harness reads. For example, prompt files and reusable tool-set files are Local harness customizations; use skills for reusable workflows with other skills-compatible harnesses.
-
-| Observed behavior | Smallest change to try |
-|-------------------|------------------------|
-| The agent misses a one-time requirement or relevant file | Add the requirement or [context](/docs/chat/copilot-chat-context.md) to the current request |
-| The agent repeatedly misses a project-wide command, convention, or architecture decision | Add or refine project instructions |
-| The problem only affects certain files, languages, or tasks | Add targeted instructions |
-| Your team repeatedly explains the same multi-step process | Create an agent skill |
-| A recurring role needs focused instructions or a restricted tool set | Create a custom agent |
-| The agent needs access to a supported service, such as Slack or Notion | Connect a [Copilot connector](/docs/agent-customization/copilot-connectors.md) `feature(copilot-connectors)` |
-| The agent needs an external integration that isn't available as a connector | Add an MCP server |
-| An action must run at a lifecycle point independently of the model | Configure a hook |
-| Your team wants to install and maintain a packaged set of customizations | Use an agent plugin |
-
-Ask the following questions when choosing a customization:
-
-* Does the selected harness support the format, file location, and scope you need?
-* Should it apply automatically, or only when you request it?
-* Are you providing guidance, defining a workflow, adding a capability, or enforcing an action?
-* Should the model decide when to use it?
-
-The following table compares the customization types by purpose and activation.
+Customization types differ in both purpose and activation. Activation determines when guidance enters a request or an action runs. Support depends on the [agent harness](/docs/agents/concepts/agent-harnesses.md), the runtime that coordinates the model and tools, rather than the language model you select.
 
 | Need | Use | Example | Activation |
 |------|-----|---------|------------|
 | Apply standards across a project | [Always-on instructions](/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions.md) | Require a specific logging library and error-handling pattern | Automatically included in each request |
-| Apply guidance to specific code or tasks | [File-based instructions](/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions.md) | Apply React conventions when the agent works with `.tsx` files | Included when files match a pattern or the task matches the description |
-| Teach the agent a workflow with supporting resources | [Agent skills](/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills.md) | Create a service from instructions, template files, and a setup script | The agent loads the skill when the task matches, or you invoke it directly |
+| Apply guidance to specific code or tasks | [File-based instructions](/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions.md) | Apply React conventions when the agent works with `.tsx` files | Included when file patterns match. In Local sessions, the agent can also load instructions by task relevance. |
+| Teach the agent a workflow with supporting resources | [Agent skills](/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills.md) | Create a service from instructions, template files, and a setup script | The agent can load a relevant skill, or you invoke it directly |
 | Run a saved task on demand | [Prompt files](/docs/agent-customization/prompt-files.md) | Scaffold a React component | You invoke the prompt as a slash command (Local harness sessions only) |
 | Use a specialized role and tool configuration | [Custom agents](/docs/agent-customization/custom-agents.md) | Review code with read-only tools | You select the agent, use it as a subagent, or another agent delegates to it |
 | Connect to an external system | Manually configured [MCP servers](/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers.md) or managed [Copilot connectors](/docs/agent-customization/copilot-connectors.md) `feature(copilot-connectors)` | Query a database or update an issue | The agent calls an MCP tool when the task requires it |
-| Run code at a lifecycle event | [Hooks](/docs/agent-customization/hooks.md) | Run a formatter after a file edit or block a risky command | VS Code runs the hook when the configured event occurs |
+| Run code at a specific point in the agent's workflow | [Hooks](/docs/agent-customization/hooks.md) | Run a formatter after a file edit or block a risky command | The harness runs the hook when the configured event occurs and its execution conditions are met |
 | Install a packaged customization setup | [Agent plugins](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md) | Add a testing workflow with a skill, agent, hooks, and MCP server | Each bundled customization follows its own activation rules |
 
-Start with instructions when your main goal is to stop repeating project context. Add other customization types when you identify a recurring task, specialized role, missing capability, or action that must always run.
+The closest alternatives differ in these ways:
+
+* **Instructions or skills**: instructions provide standing guidance, such as project conventions. A skill describes how to perform a particular task and can include scripts, templates, and other resources.
+* **Skills or prompt files**: a skill can be discovered for a relevant task or invoked directly. A prompt file is a saved prompt that you invoke explicitly in a Local harness session.
+* **Skills or custom agents**: a skill supplies a workflow. A custom agent defines the role and tool configuration that performs work, and can use skills as part of that work.
+* **Instructions or custom agents**: an `AGENTS.md` file gives guidance to an existing agent. Despite its name, it doesn't define a custom agent.
+
+For supported services, Copilot connectors provide managed MCP connections without local server setup or configuration files. Use a manually configured MCP server when you need another integration or its configuration options.
+
+You don't need a customization for a one-time requirement. Add it to the current request instead. When a problem repeats, [choose the smallest useful customization](/docs/agent-customization/overview.md#choose-how-to-customize).
+
+## Marketplaces and reusable customizations
+
+You don't need to author every customization yourself. Marketplaces help you discover existing workflows and integrations from community publishers or your organization.
+
+* **Customizations** are the instructions, workflows, tools, and other building blocks an agent uses.
+* **Plugins** package related customizations for installation together. A plugin can include skills, custom agents, hooks, and MCP servers.
+* **Plugin marketplaces** are catalogs of plugins. Adding a marketplace makes its plugins available to browse. Installing a plugin makes its supported components available to your harness.
+
+The **Customization Marketplace** is the unified **Browse** experience in the Agent Customizations editor (Preview). It brings together supported sources, including plugin marketplaces, GitHub Feed, and Copilot connectors `feature(copilot-connectors)`. Some sources offer individual skills or MCP servers; others offer plugins that bundle customizations. Available sources depend on the harness and organization policy.
+
+A marketplace is a discovery and distribution mechanism, not another customization type. Installed components keep their own activation rules. Review the publisher, included files, and setup requirements before installation, then test the result in your workflow. See [Discover and install existing customizations](/docs/agent-customization/overview.md#discover-and-install-existing-customizations-preview).
 
 ## Model-driven vs. deterministic behavior
 
 Most customizations guide the model or give it more options. The model interprets instructions, decides whether a skill is relevant, and chooses when to call an available tool. The result depends on the request, available context, and model reasoning.
 
-Hooks are dispatched by the runtime when a supported, configured lifecycle event occurs. Use a hook for actions such as validating a tool call or starting a formatter after an edit. Discovery, trust, filters, timeouts, and error handling still affect execution. Use instructions when you want to guide how the agent reasons or writes code.
+The runtime triggers a hook when its configured event occurs, such as a tool call starting or finishing. Use a hook for actions such as validating a tool call or starting a formatter after an edit. Discovery, trust, filters, timeouts, and error handling still affect execution. Use instructions when you want to guide how the agent reasons or writes code.
 
-For example, an instruction that says "run the formatter after editing a file" asks the model to remember and perform that action. A hook configured for the corresponding lifecycle event runs regardless of whether the model remembers the instruction.
-
-For new Copilot hooks, use the [shared runtime guidance](/docs/agent-customization/hooks.md). Existing hooks in personal folders, settings, repositories, agents, or plugins need a [compatibility review](/docs/agent-customization/migrate-customizations.md#migrate-hooks) when migrating from Local.
+For example, an instruction that says "run the formatter after editing a file" asks the model to remember and perform that action. A hook configured to run after the editing tool completes performs that action regardless of whether the model remembers the instruction.

 The fields below describe the VS Code format. Files in `.claude/agents` use the [Claude agent format](#claude-agent-format).
 
+## Custom agent file locations
+
+You can define custom agents for a specific workspace or at the user level, where they are available across your workspaces. Select the intended harness before you create an agent so the Agent Customizations editor stores it in a supported location.
+
+| Scope | Default file location | File format |
+|-------|-----------------------|-------------|
+| Workspace | `.github/agents` folder | `.agent.md` or `.md` files |
+| Workspace (Claude format) | `.claude/agents` folder | `.md` files in the [Claude agent format](#claude-agent-format) |
+| User (Copilot) | `~/.copilot/agents` folder | `.agent.md` or `.md` files |
+| User ([product.prodname_anthropic_claude]) | `~/.claude/agents` folder | `.md` files in the [Claude agent format](#claude-agent-format) |
+
+To create a user-level custom agent, use the Agent Customizations editor or the **Chat: New Custom Agent** command. Store the file in a supported folder on the machine where the selected harness runs.
+
+In a monorepo, enable ``chat.useCustomizationsInParentRepositories`` to discover custom agents from the parent repository root. Learn more about [parent repository discovery](/docs/agent-customization/overview.md#use-customizations-in-a-monorepo).
+
+### Local harness locations and migration
+
+The **Local** harness stores user-level custom agents in VS Code profile storage, separate from harness user folders such as `~/.copilot/agents` and `~/.claude/agents`. To reuse profile-based agents with another harness, [move them to that harness's user folder](/docs/agent-customization/migrate-customizations.md#move-user-agents-and-instructions).
+
+Prefer native harness folders, such as `.github/agents` and `~/.copilot/agents`, over custom search locations. The ``chat.agentFilesLocations`` setting remains supported and is not deprecated. The editor forwards agents from additional configured locations to Agent Host harnesses, including Copilot, for compatibility with existing editor workflows. The older `chat.modeFilesLocations` setting is deprecated.
+
+Custom locations are not recommended for Copilot workflows because GitHub Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app do not inherit editor location settings. To use agents across Copilot clients, [move them to native harness locations](/docs/agent-customization/migrate-customizations.md#move-customizations-from-configured-locations).
+
+Custom agents were previously known as custom chat modes. If you have `.chatmode.md` files, rename them to `.agent.md` and place them in a supported custom agent location.
+
+If an agent has `hooks` in its frontmatter, review the [agent-scoped hook contract](/docs/agent-customization/hooks.md#agent-scoped-hooks). VS Code preserves those hooks when converting agents for Copilot, including plugin-provided agents. Keep agent-specific automation scoped to the agent and verify that its hooks run before completing a migration.
+
+### Organization-level agents
+
+To share custom agents across multiple workspaces within your organization, you can define them at the GitHub organization level.
+
+VS Code automatically detects organization-level custom agents to which your account has access. These agents appear in the agents dropdown alongside built-in, personal, and workspace agents.
+
+Discovery of organization-level custom agents is enabled by default. To stop showing them in chat, set ``github.copilot.chat.organizationCustomAgents.enabled`` to `false`.
+
+Learn how to [create custom agents for your organization](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/coding-agent/create-custom-agents) in the GitHub documentation.
+
 ## Harness compatibility
 
 The selected [agent harness](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md) determines which fields and tool names take effect. A shared file location does not imply identical behavior across harnesses.

 The editor identifies attributes that aren't supported by the effective target. For example, Local doesn't accept `skills` or `mcp-servers`, and Copilot doesn't accept `handoffs`, `agents`, `argument-hint`, or `advancedOptions`.
+
+### Edit a custom agent file
+
+Use completions and hover details in an `.agent.md` file to choose values for the intended harness. An explicit `target` overrides how the editor interprets the file, but doesn't switch your session's harness.
+
+For Copilot-assisted editing, set `target` explicitly when you need target-specific guidance. Without an explicit target, the file context supplied to Copilot describes only shared attributes and doesn't suggest target-specific model or tool values. This differs from normal editor completions, which follow the selected harness.
+
+Hover a value to inspect its details or availability. The editor refreshes validation as harness inventories change. Unknown-value hints depend on discovery completing, so the absence of a hint while discovery is pending doesn't confirm that a value is available.
+
+Select the intended harness before editing, then try the agent in that harness to verify its behavior. Editor feedback doesn't replace checking which tools and skills the running agent can use. See [Verify your custom agent](/docs/agent-customization/custom-agents.md#verify-your-custom-agent).

->         version="v3",
->     )
->     for snapshot in stream.values:
->         print(snapshot)
->
->     stream = graph.stream_events(
->         {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "what's my name?"}]},
->         config,  # [!code highlight]
->         version="v3",
->     )
->     for snapshot in stream.values:
->         print(snapshot)
-> ```
->
-> **Async**
->
-> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-> from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
-> from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, MessagesState, START
-> from langgraph.checkpoint.postgres.aio import AsyncPostgresSaver  # [!code highlight]
->
-> model = init_chat_model(model="claude-haiku-4-5-20251001")
->
-> DB_URI = "postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable"
-> async with AsyncPostgresSaver.from_conn_string(DB_URI) as checkpointer:  # [!code highlight]
->     # await checkpointer.setup()
->
->     async def call_model(state: MessagesState):
->         response = await model.ainvoke(state["messages"])
->         return {"messages": response}
->
->     builder = StateGraph(MessagesState)
->     builder.add_node(call_model)
->     builder.add_edge(START, "call_model")
->
->     graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)  # [!code highlight]
->
->     config = {
->         "configurable": {
->             "thread_id": "1"  # [!code highlight]
->         }
->     }
->
->     stream = await graph.astream_events(
->         {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi! I'm bob"}]},
->         config,  # [!code highlight]
->         version="v3",
->     )
->     async for message in stream.messages:
->         async for token in message.text:
->             print(token, end="", flush=True)
->
->     stream = await graph.astream_events(
->         {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "what's my name?"}]},
->         config,  # [!code highlight]
->         version="v3",
->     )
->     async for message in stream.messages:
->         async for token in message.text:
->             print(token, end="", flush=True)
-> ```
-
-> **Example: using MongoDB checkpointer**
+> > [tab] Sync
+> >
+> > ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
+> > from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
+> > from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, MessagesState, START
+> > from langgraph.checkpoint.postgres import PostgresSaver  # [!code highlight]
+> >
+> > model = init_chat_model(model="claude-haiku-4-5-20251001")
+> >
+> > DB_URI = "postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable"

Isolated to the default agent’s tool schemas, total description tokens drop `,_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`43%`}),` (4,005 → 2,302); combined with the empty base prompt and opt-in todos, a default-agent turn’s input tokens drop `,_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`65%`}),` (5,395 → 1,895). Tool behavior is unchanged. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4859`,children:`#4859`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4979`,children:`#4979`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/5009`,children:`#5009`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`features-3`,children:`Features`}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/customization#middleware`,children:`Override a default middleware instance`})}),`: A `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware=`}),` (or subagent `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware`}),`) instance whose `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`.name`}),` matches a built-in now replaces that default in place, rather than erroring on a duplicate. For example, pass your own `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`SummarizationMiddleware(...)`}),` to change the token trigger or summary model without disabling the built-in default. `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`write_file`}),` now overwrites an existing file instead of erroring (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4109`,children:`#4109`}),`); and reads and searches are tuned for open models — paginated `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`read_file`}),` reports total and remaining lines plus the next `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`offset`}),` (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4540`,children:`#4540`}),`), `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`grep`}),`/`,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`glob`}),` return partial results with a `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`truncated`}),` flag instead of hanging on large trees (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4063`,children:`#4063`}),`), and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`grep`}),` gains a 1,000-match cap with streamed output and optional context lines (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4570`,children:`#4570`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4706`,children:`#4706`}),`).`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`More prompt-caching support`}),`: Bedrock prompt caching via the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents[aws]`}),` extra (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/issues/4108`,children:`#4108`}),`), and automatic Fireworks prompt-cache session affinity (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4598`,children:`#4598`}),`).`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`NVIDIA support`}),`: A built-in Nemotron 3 Ultra harness profile plus NIM app-origin attribution. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4561`,children:`#4561`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(_components.p,{children:`Copy the following prompt into your AI coding assistant to migrate a codebase for these breaking changes:`}),_jsx(Prompt,{description:`Migrate a deepagents codebase from v0.6.x to v0.7.`,icon:`arrow-right`,actions:[`copy`],children:'Migrate this codebase from `deepagents` v0.6.x to v0.7 to account for the following breaking changes:\\n\\n1. `create_deep_agent` no longer includes `TodoListMiddleware` by default. If this codebase relies on the `write_todos` tool, the `todos` state channel, or the todo-planning prompt, restore it by importing `TodoListMiddleware` from `langchain.agents.middleware` (not `deepagents`) and passing it to `create_deep_agent`:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from langchain.agents.middleware import TodoListMiddleware\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()])\\n   ```\\n\\n2. Backend compatibility shims were removed: `BackendFactory`, `BACKEND_TYPES`, `FileFormat`, and `Unset` no longer exist. Replace any backend factories with concrete `BackendProtocol` instances, and add an explicit `namespace` to every `StoreBackend` configuration:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n   from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\\n\\n   # Before (v0.6.x): factory callable, and StoreBackend with no explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend())  # [!code --]\\n\\n   # After (v0.7): concrete backend instance with an explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)))  # [!code ++]\\n   ```\\n\\n   Also update calls to use the current `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, and `ReadResult` APIs.\\n\\n3. Tool output formats changed: empty `ls` / `glob` output is now the string `No files found` instead of `[]`, and `read_file` no longer renders a fixed-width `cat -n`-style line-number gutter. On a default-agent turn, input tokens drop `,_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`65%`}),` (5,395 → 1,895), validated against our `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://www.langchain.com/blog/how-we-benchmark-deep-agents`,children:`revamped evaluation suite`}),` with no quality regression.`]}),_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`optimizations`,children:`Optimizations`}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Lean prompts by default`}),`: The authored base prompt starts empty and tool-usage prose that duplicated tool schemas has been trimmed. Isolated to the default agent’s tool schemas, total description tokens drop `,_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`43%`}),` (4,005 → 2,302); combined with the empty base prompt and opt-in todos, a default-agent turn’s input tokens drop `,_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`65%`}),` (5,395 → 1,895). Tool behavior is unchanged. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4859`,children:`#4859`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4979`,children:`#4979`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/5009`,children:`#5009`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`features-3`,children:`Features`}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/customization#middleware`,children:`Override a default middleware instance`})}),`: A `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware=`}),` (or subagent `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware`}),`) instance whose `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`.name`}),` matches a built-in now replaces that default in place, rather than erroring on a duplicate. For example, pass your own `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`SummarizationMiddleware(...)`}),` to change the token trigger or summary model without disabling the built-in default. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4251`,children:`#4251`}),`)`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Filesystem tools`}),`: New `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/tools#built-in-harness-tools`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`delete`})}),` tool removes a file or recursively removes a directory (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/3659`,children:`#3659`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/3851`,children:`#3851`}),`); `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`write_file`}),` now overwrites an existing file instead of erroring (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4109`,children:`#4109`}),`); `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`FilesystemMiddleware`}),` accepts a `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/overview#virtual-filesystem-access`,children:`tool allowlist`}),` to expose only selected built-in tools (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4325`,children:`#4325`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4698`,children:`#4698`}),`); and reads and searches are tuned for open models — paginated `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`read_file`}),` reports total and remaining lines plus the next `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`offset`}),` (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4540`,children:`#4540`}),`), `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`grep`}),`/`,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`glob`}),` return partial results with a `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`truncated`}),` flag instead of hanging on large trees (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4063`,children:`#4063`}),`), and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`grep`}),` gains a 1,000-match cap with streamed output and optional context lines (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4570`,children:`#4570`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4706`,children:`#4706`}),`).`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`More prompt-caching support`}),`: Bedrock prompt caching via the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents[aws]`}),` extra (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/issues/4108`,children:`#4108`}),`), and automatic Fireworks prompt-cache session affinity (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4598`,children:`#4598`}),`).`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`NVIDIA support`}),`: A built-in Nemotron 3 Ultra harness profile plus NIM app-origin attribution. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4192`,children:`#4192`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4455`,children:`#4455`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`breaking-changes-2`,children:`Breaking changes`}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Planning todos are opt-in`}),`: `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`create_deep_agent`}),` no longer includes `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`TodoListMiddleware`}),` by default, so the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`write_todos`}),` tool, `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`todos`}),` state channel, and todo-planning prompt are absent unless restored with `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()]`}),`. (The OpenAI Codex harness profile still opts in automatically.) (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4929`,children:`#4929`}),`)`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Backend compatibility shims removed`}),`: Pass concrete `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`BackendProtocol`}),` instances instead of factories, configure `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`StoreBackend`}),` with an explicit `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`namespace`}),`, and use the current `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`ls`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`glob`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`grep`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`ReadResult`}),` APIs. Removed symbols include `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`BackendFactory`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`BACKEND_TYPES`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`FileFormat`}),`, and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Unset`}),`. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4541`,children:`#4541`}),`)`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Output format changes`}),`: Empty `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`ls`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`glob`}),` output is now `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`No files found`}),` instead of `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`[]`}),`, and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`read_file`}),` no longer renders a fixed-width `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`cat -n`}),`-style gutter — update any parsers of raw tool output. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4561`,children:`#4561`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(_components.p,{children:`Copy the following prompt into your AI coding assistant to migrate a codebase for these breaking changes:`}),_jsx(Prompt,{description:`Migrate a deepagents codebase from v0.6.x to v0.7.`,icon:`arrow-right`,actions:[`copy`],children:'Migrate this codebase from `deepagents` v0.6.x to v0.7 to account for the following breaking changes:\\n\\n1. `create_deep_agent` no longer includes `TodoListMiddleware` by default. If this codebase relies on the `write_todos` tool, the `todos` state channel, or the todo-planning prompt, restore it by importing `TodoListMiddleware` from `langchain.agents.middleware` (not `deepagents`) and passing it to `create_deep_agent`:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from langchain.agents.middleware import TodoListMiddleware\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()])\\n   ```\\n\\n2. Backend compatibility shims were removed: `BackendFactory`, `BACKEND_TYPES`, `FileFormat`, and `Unset` no longer exist. Replace any backend factories with concrete `BackendProtocol` instances, and add an explicit `namespace` to every `StoreBackend` configuration:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n   from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\\n\\n   # Before (v0.6.x): factory callable, and StoreBackend with no explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend())  # [!code --]\\n\\n   # After (v0.7): concrete backend instance with an explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)))  # [!code ++]\\n   ```\\n\\n   Also update calls to use the current `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, and `ReadResult` APIs.\\n\\n3. Tool output formats changed: empty `ls` / `glob` output is now the string `No files found` instead of `[]`, and `read_file` no longer renders a fixed-width `cat -n`-style line-number gutter. Update any code that parses these tool outputs.\\n\\nSearch the codebase for usages of the removed symbols and for parsing logic that depends on the old output formats, apply the necessary changes, and flag anything that needs manual review.\\n'})]}),`\n`,_jsxs(Update,{label:`May 12, 2026`,tags:[`deepagents`],rss:{title:`May 12, 2026 - langchain`},id:`may-12%2C-2026`,children:[_jsxs(Heading,{level:`2`,id:`deepagents-v0-6-0`,children:[_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents`}),` v0.6.0`]}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/interpreters`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CodeInterpreterMiddleware`})})}),`: (experimental) `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents`}),` now supports code execution and programmatic tool calling through a scoped QuickJS runtime.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[`Supports `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`version=\"v3\"`}),` in `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`stream_events`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`astream_events`}),`. Rather than re-serializing the full accumulated value into every checkpoint, only the incremental delta written at each step is stored — keeping checkpoint sizes small as threads grow long.`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(Warning,{children:_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Rolling back from v0.6.0 is not supported once threads have persisted.`}),` Deep Agents v0.6.0 changes persisted message history and agent files to `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`DeltaChannel`}),`, which writes checkpoints in a new format that earlier versions cannot read. Downgrading to an earlier Deep Agents version switches these channels back to non-delta channels, leaving existing delta checkpoints unreadable and causing incomplete or incorrect state reconstruction. If you need to roll back, use the `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/tree/main/examples/delta-channel-dump`,children:`delta-channel-dump recovery script`}),` to migrate affected threads, or discard them, before downgrading. More generally, avoid switching a persisted channel between delta and non-delta representations. See `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/langgraph/pregel#version-compatibility-and-rollbacks`,children:`Version compatibility and channel changes`}),`.`]})}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/profiles`,children:`Harness profiles`})}),`: Register per-provider or per-model configuration bundles (`,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`HarnessProfile`}),`) that `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`create_deep_agent`}),` applies automatically when a model is selected — system-prompt tweaks, tool overrides, middleware changes, and subagent defaults — without modifying the call site.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/backends#contexthubbackend`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`ContextHubBackend`})})}),` (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://www.langchain.com/blog/introducing-context-hub`,children:`blog`}),`): A new filesystem backend backed by LangSmith Hub. Most useful for channels that grow large over time, for example a message list in a long-running thread. Use `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`snapshot_frequency=K`}),` to write a full snapshot every K steps and bound read latency.`]}),`\n`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/langgraph/fault-tolerance#timeouts`,children:`Per-node timeouts`})}),`: Pass `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`timeout=`}),` to `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph/graph/state/StateGraph/add_node`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`add_node`})}),` to cap how long a single attempt may run. If this codebase relies on the `write_todos` tool, the `todos` state channel, or the todo-planning prompt, restore it by importing `TodoListMiddleware` from `langchain.agents.middleware` (not `deepagents`) and passing it to `create_deep_agent`:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from langchain.agents.middleware import TodoListMiddleware\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()])\\n   ```\\n\\n2. Backend compatibility shims were removed: `BackendFactory`, `BACKEND_TYPES`, `FileFormat`, and `Unset` no longer exist. Replace any backend factories with concrete `BackendProtocol` instances, and add an explicit `namespace` to every `StoreBackend` configuration:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n   from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\\n\\n   # Before (v0.6.x): factory callable, and StoreBackend with no explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend())  # [!code --]\\n\\n   # After (v0.7): concrete backend instance with an explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)))  # [!code ++]\\n   ```\\n\\n   Also update calls to use the current `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, and `ReadResult` APIs.\\n\\n3. Tool output formats changed: empty `ls` / `glob` output is now the string `No files found` instead of `[]`, and `read_file` no longer renders a fixed-width `cat -n`-style line-number gutter. If this codebase relies on the `write_todos` tool, the `todos` state channel, or the todo-planning prompt, restore it by importing `TodoListMiddleware` from `langchain.agents.middleware` (not `deepagents`) and passing it to `create_deep_agent`:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from langchain.agents.middleware import TodoListMiddleware\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()])\\n   ```\\n\\n2. Backend compatibility shims were removed: `BackendFactory`, `BACKEND_TYPES`, `FileFormat`, and `Unset` no longer exist. Replace any backend factories with concrete `BackendProtocol` instances, and add an explicit `namespace` to every `StoreBackend` configuration:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n   from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\\n\\n   # Before (v0.6.x): factory callable, and StoreBackend with no explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend())  # [!code --]\\n\\n   # After (v0.7): concrete backend instance with an explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)))  # [!code ++]\\n   ```\\n\\n   Also update calls to use the current `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, and `ReadResult` APIs.\\n\\n3. Tool output formats changed: empty `ls` / `glob` output is now the string `No files found` instead of `[]`, and `read_file` no longer renders a fixed-width `cat -n`-style line-number gutter. Update any code that parses these tool outputs.\\n\\nSearch the codebase for usages of the removed symbols and for parsing logic that depends on the old output formats, apply the necessary changes, and flag anything that needs manual review.\\n'})]}),`\n`,_jsxs(Update,{label:`May 12, 2026`,tags:[`deepagents`],rss:{title:`May 12, 2026 - langchain`},id:`may-12%2C-2026`,children:[_jsxs(Heading,{level:`2`,id:`deepagents-v0-6-0`,children:[_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents`}),` v0.6.0`]}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/interpreters`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CodeInterpreterMiddleware`})})}),`: (experimental) `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents`}),` now supports code execution and programmatic tool calling through a scoped QuickJS runtime.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[`Supports `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`version=\"v3\"`}),` in `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`stream_events`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`astream_events`}),`.  In this example, an invalid answer causes the node to return the updated question. During the same graph run, the conditional edge invokes the node again, and this new invocation pauses at `interrupt()`.  >
 > Static interrupts are **not** recommended for human-in-the-loop workflows. Use the [`interrupt`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph/types/interrupt) function instead.
 
-**At compile time**
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-graph = builder.compile(
-    interrupt_before=["node_a"],  # [!code highlight]
-    interrupt_after=["node_b", "node_c"],  # [!code highlight]
-    checkpointer=checkpointer,
-)
-
-# Pass a thread ID to the graph
-config = {
-    "configurable": {
-        "thread_id": "some_thread"
-    }
-}
-
-# Run the graph until the breakpoint
-graph.invoke(inputs, config=config)  # [!code highlight]
-
-# Resume the graph
-graph.invoke(None, config=config)  # [!code highlight]
-```
-
-1. The breakpoints are set during `compile` time.
-2. `interrupt_before` specifies the nodes where execution should pause before the node is executed.
-3. `interrupt_after` specifies the nodes where execution should pause after the node is executed.
-4. A checkpointer is required to enable breakpoints.
-5. The graph is run until the first breakpoint is hit.
-6. The graph is resumed by passing in `None` for the input. This will run the graph until the next breakpoint is hit.
-
-**At run time**
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}

 If a [node](#nodes) contains multiple operations, you may find it easier to implement each operation as a [**task**](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/functional-api.md#task) instead of splitting the logic across multiple nodes. Task results are checkpointed when the graph uses a checkpointer, so resuming a thread can skip completed **task** work inside the node.
 
-**Original**
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}

-
-import requests
-from langchain_core.utils.uuid import uuid7

-
-class State(TypedDict):
-    url: str
-    result: NotRequired[str]
-
-def call_api(state: State):
-    """Example node that makes an API request."""
-    result = requests.get(state["url"]).text[:100]  # [!code highlight]
-    return {"result": result}
-
-builder = StateGraph(State)
-builder.add_node("call_api", call_api)
-builder.add_edge(START, "call_api")
-builder.add_edge("call_api", END)
-
-checkpointer = InMemorySaver()
-graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)
-
-thread_id = str(uuid7())
-config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}}
-
-graph.invoke({"url": "https://www.example.com"}, config)

-

-> Open a public LangSmith run for this example.

-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}

-
-import requests
-from langchain_core.utils.uuid import uuid7
-from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
-from langgraph.func import task
-from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
-from typing_extensions import TypedDict
-
-class State(TypedDict):
-    urls: list[str]
-    results: NotRequired[list[str]]
-
-@task
-def _make_request(url: str):
-    """Make a request."""
-    return requests.get(url).text[:100]  # [!code highlight]
-
-def call_api(state: State):
-    """Example node that makes API requests as checkpointed tasks."""
-    futures = [_make_request(url) for url in state["urls"]]  # [!code highlight]
-    results = [f.result() for f in futures]
-    return {"results": results}
-
-builder = StateGraph(State)
-builder.add_node("call_api", call_api)
-builder.add_edge(START, "call_api")
-builder.add_edge("call_api", END)
-
-checkpointer = InMemorySaver()
-graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)
-
-thread_id = str(uuid7())
-config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}}
-

### [MODIFICADO] `langgraph::quickstart`
- **URL Canónica**: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/quickstart
- **Hash Anterior**: `fa52d3638e6264bcc50456bc2b0544e52af637a70ab6097c71cec03212b3bc16`
- **Hash Nuevo**: `6595a22968246e150d0faf2114857ec03f709e0f0ed5447c9dacc550f765b490`

```diff
--- langgraph::quickstart (prev: fa52d363)
+++ langgraph::quickstart (new: 6595a229)
@@ -89,192 +89,13 @@
 >
 > For this example, you will need to set up a [Claude (Anthropic)](https://www.anthropic.com/) account and get an API key. Then, set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in your terminal. See [chat model integrations](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/integrations/chat.md) for all available providers. Alternatively, If you are using the LangSmith [LLM Gateway](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/llm-gateway.md), traffic to providers is routed through LangSmith. Use the gateway key as the API key instead.
 
-**Use the Graph API**
-
-## 1. Define tools and model
-
-In this example, we'll use the Claude Sonnet 4.5 model and define tools for addition, multiplication, and division.
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-from langchain.tools import tool
-from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
-
-model = init_chat_model(
-    "claude-sonnet-4-6",
-    temperature=0
-)
-
-# Define tools
-@tool
-def multiply(a: int, b: int) -> int:
-    """Multiply `a` and `b`.
-
-    Args:
-        a: First int
-        b: Second int
-    """
-    return a * b
-
-@tool
-def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
-    """Adds `a` and `b`.
-
-    Args:
-        a: First int
-        b: Second int
-    """
-    return a + b
-
-@tool
-def divide(a: int, b: int) -> float:
-    """Divide `a` and `b`.
-
-    Args:
-        a: First int
-        b: Second int
-    """
-    return a / b
-
-# Augment the LLM with tools
-tools = [add, multiply, divide]
-tools_by_name = {tool.name: tool for tool in tools}
-model_with_tools = model.bind_tools(tools)
-```
-
-## 2. Define state
-
-The graph's state is used to store the messages and the number of LLM calls.
-
-> [!TIP]
->
-> State in LangGraph persists throughout the agent's execution.
->
-> The `Annotated` type with `operator.add` ensures that new messages are appended to the existing list rather than replacing it.
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-from langchain.messages import AnyMessage
-from typing_extensions import TypedDict, Annotated
-import operator
-
-class MessagesState(TypedDict):
-    messages: Annotated[list[AnyMessage], operator.add]
-    llm_calls: int
-```
-
-## 3. Define model node
-
-The model node is used to call the LLM and decide whether to call a tool or not.
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-from langchain.messages import SystemMessage
-
-def llm_call(state: dict):
-    """LLM decides whether to call a tool or not"""
-
-    return {
-        "messages": [
-            model_with_tools.invoke(
-                [
-                    SystemMessage(
-                        content="You are a helpful assistant tasked with performing arithmetic on a set of inputs."
-                    )
-                ]
-                + state["messages"]
-            )
-        ],
-        "llm_calls": state.get('llm_calls', 0) + 1
-    }
-```
-
-## 4. Define tool node
-
-The tool node is used to call the tools and return the results.
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-from langchain.messages import ToolMessage
-
-def tool_node(state: dict):
-    """Performs the tool call"""
-
-    result = []
-    for tool_call in state["messages"][-1].tool_calls:
-        tool = tools_by_name[tool_call["name"]]
-        observation = tool.invoke(tool_call["args"])
-        result.append(ToolMessage(content=observation, tool_call_id=tool_call["id"]))
-    return {"messages": result}
-```
```

### [MODIFICADO] `langgraph::pregel`
- **URL Canónica**: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/pregel
- **Hash Anterior**: `ed1e14eadd09a347c15995633961ce72e3a4188d2e5ed50f9387d89418ca05f8`
- **Hash Nuevo**: `02b5686596e2e0f8fa9bf02333a83945db5b867a822be6df8f576ab7f2578626`

```diff
--- langgraph::pregel (prev: ed1e14ea)
+++ langgraph::pregel (new: 02b56865)
@@ -170,294 +170,297 @@
 
 Below are a few different examples to give you a sense of the Pregel API.
 
-**Single node**
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-from langgraph.channels import EphemeralValue
-from langgraph.pregel import Pregel, NodeBuilder
-
-node1 = (
-    NodeBuilder().subscribe_only("a")
-    .do(lambda x: x + x)
-    .write_to("b")
-)
-
-app = Pregel(
-    nodes={"node1": node1},
-    channels={
-        "a": EphemeralValue(str),
-        "b": EphemeralValue(str),
-    },
-    input_channels=["a"],
-    output_channels=["b"],
-)
-
-app.invoke({"a": "foo"})
-```
-
-```con theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-{'b': 'foofoo'}
-```
-
-**Multiple nodes**
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-from langgraph.channels import LastValue, EphemeralValue
-from langgraph.pregel import Pregel, NodeBuilder
-
-node1 = (
-    NodeBuilder().subscribe_only("a")
-    .do(lambda x: x + x)
-    .write_to("b")
-)
-
-node2 = (
-    NodeBuilder().subscribe_only("b")
-    .do(lambda x: x + x)
-    .write_to("c")
-)
-
-app = Pregel(
-    nodes={"node1": node1, "node2": node2},
-    channels={
-        "a": EphemeralValue(str),
-        "b": LastValue(str),
-        "c": EphemeralValue(str),
-    },
-    input_channels=["a"],
-    output_channels=["b", "c"],
-)
-
-app.invoke({"a": "foo"})
-```
-
-```con theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-{'b': 'foofoo', 'c': 'foofoofoofoo'}
-```
-
-**Topic**
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-from langgraph.channels import EphemeralValue, Topic
-from langgraph.pregel import Pregel, NodeBuilder
-
-node1 = (
-    NodeBuilder().subscribe_only("a")
-    .do(lambda x: x + x)
-    .write_to("b", "c")
-)
-
-node2 = (
-    NodeBuilder().subscribe_to("b")
-    .do(lambda x: x["b"] + x["b"])
-    .write_to("c")
-)
-
-app = Pregel(
-    nodes={"node1": node1, "node2": node2},
-    channels={
-        "a": EphemeralValue(str),
-        "b": EphemeralValue(str),
-        "c": Topic(str, accumulate=True),
-    },
-    input_channels=["a"],
-    output_channels=["c"],
-)
-
-app.invoke({"a": "foo"})
-```
-
-```pycon theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-{'c': ['foofoo', 'foofoofoofoo']}
-```
-
-**BinaryOperatorAggregate**
-
-This example demonstrates how to use the [`BinaryOperatorAggregate`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph/channels/binop/BinaryOperatorAggregate) channel to implement a reducer.
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-from langgraph.channels import EphemeralValue, BinaryOperatorAggregate
-from langgraph.pregel import Pregel, NodeBuilder
-
-node1 = (
-    NodeBuilder().subscribe_only("a")
-    .do(lambda x: x + x)
-    .write_to("b", "c")
-)
```

### [MODIFICADO] `langgraph::use-time-travel`
- **URL Canónica**: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/use-time-travel
- **Hash Anterior**: `2be4640f2f4704a62cc3e4cfab575eb9320c524d0064cb5e0b7977a5d35c6458`
- **Hash Nuevo**: `bbde1d5956d8a775d410e5274ee0ccea7388a61f461eac0a8aa6ca5c223edd53`

```diff
--- langgraph::use-time-travel (prev: 2be4640f)
+++ langgraph::use-time-travel (new: bbde1d59)
@@ -200,88 +200,88 @@
 
 Time travel with [subgraphs](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/use-subgraphs.md) depends on whether the subgraph has its own checkpointer. This determines the granularity of checkpoints you can time travel from.
 
-**Inherited checkpointer (default)**
-
-By default, a subgraph inherits the parent's checkpointer. The parent treats the entire subgraph as a **single super-step** — there is only one parent-level checkpoint for the whole subgraph execution. Time traveling from before the subgraph re-executes it from scratch.
-
-You cannot time travel to a point *between* nodes in a default subgraph — you can only time travel from the parent level.
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-# Subgraph without its own checkpointer (default)
-subgraph = (
-    StateGraph(State)
-    .add_node("step_a", step_a)       # Has interrupt()
-    .add_node("step_b", step_b)       # Has interrupt()
-    .add_edge(START, "step_a")
-    .add_edge("step_a", "step_b")
-    .compile()  # No checkpointer — inherits from parent
-)
-
-graph = (
-    StateGraph(State)
-    .add_node("subgraph_node", subgraph)
-    .add_edge(START, "subgraph_node")
-    .compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())
-)
-
-config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
-
-# Complete both interrupts
-graph.invoke({"value": []}, config)            # Hits step_a interrupt
-graph.invoke(Command(resume="Alice"), config)  # Hits step_b interrupt
-graph.invoke(Command(resume="30"), config)     # Completes
-
-# Time travel from before the subgraph
-history = list(graph.get_state_history(config))
-before_sub = [s for s in history if s.next == ("subgraph_node",)][-1]
-
-fork_config = graph.update_state(before_sub.config, {"value": ["forked"]})
-result = graph.invoke(None, fork_config)
-# The entire subgraph re-executes from scratch
-# You cannot time travel to a point between step_a and step_b
-```
-
-**Subgraph checkpointer**
-
-Set `checkpointer=True` on the subgraph to give it its own checkpoint history. This creates checkpoints at each step **within** the subgraph, allowing you to time travel from a specific point inside it — for example, between two interrupts.
-
-Use [`get_state`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.CompiledStateGraph.get_state) with `subgraphs=True` to access the subgraph's own checkpoint config, then fork from it:
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-# Subgraph with its own checkpointer
-subgraph = (
-    StateGraph(State)
-    .add_node("step_a", step_a)       # Has interrupt()
-    .add_node("step_b", step_b)       # Has interrupt()
-    .add_edge(START, "step_a")
-    .add_edge("step_a", "step_b")
-    .compile(checkpointer=True)  # Own checkpoint history
-)
-
-graph = (
-    StateGraph(State)
-    .add_node("subgraph_node", subgraph)
-    .add_edge(START, "subgraph_node")
-    .compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())
-)
-
-config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
-
-# Run until step_a interrupt
-graph.invoke({"value": []}, config)
-
-# Resume step_a -> hits step_b interrupt
-graph.invoke(Command(resume="Alice"), config)
-
-# Get the subgraph's own checkpoint (between step_a and step_b)
-parent_state = graph.get_state(config, subgraphs=True)
-sub_config = parent_state.tasks[0].state.config
-
-# Fork from the subgraph checkpoint
-fork_config = graph.update_state(sub_config, {"value": ["forked"]})
-result = graph.invoke(None, fork_config)
-# step_b re-executes, step_a's result is preserved
-```
+> [tab] Inherited checkpointer (default)
+>
+> By default, a subgraph inherits the parent's checkpointer. The parent treats the entire subgraph as a **single super-step** — there is only one parent-level checkpoint for the whole subgraph execution. Time traveling from before the subgraph re-executes it from scratch.
+>
+> You cannot time travel to a point *between* nodes in a default subgraph — you can only time travel from the parent level.
+>
+> ```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
+> # Subgraph without its own checkpointer (default)
+> subgraph = (
+>     StateGraph(State)
+>     .add_node("step_a", step_a)       # Has interrupt()
+>     .add_node("step_b", step_b)       # Has interrupt()
+>     .add_edge(START, "step_a")
+>     .add_edge("step_a", "step_b")
+>     .compile()  # No checkpointer — inherits from parent
+> )
+>
+> graph = (
+>     StateGraph(State)
+>     .add_node("subgraph_node", subgraph)
+>     .add_edge(START, "subgraph_node")
+>     .compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())
+> )
+>
+> config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
+>
+> # Complete both interrupts
+> graph.invoke({"value": []}, config)            # Hits step_a interrupt
+> graph.invoke(Command(resume="Alice"), config)  # Hits step_b interrupt
+> graph.invoke(Command(resume="30"), config)     # Completes
+>
+> # Time travel from before the subgraph
```

-**Interrupts**
-
-Each invocation can use `interrupt()` to pause and resume. Add `interrupt()` to a tool function to require user approval before proceeding:
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-@tool
-def fruit_info(fruit_name: str) -> str:
-    """Look up fruit info."""
-    interrupt("continue?")  # [!code highlight]
-    return f"Info about {fruit_name}"
-```
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-from langgraph.types import Command
-
-config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
-
-# Stream events - the subagent's tool calls interrupt()
-stream = agent.stream_events(
-    {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me about apples"}]},
-    config=config,
-    version="v3",
-)
-output = stream.output  # drive the stream to completion
-# stream.interrupts contains pending interrupts (and stream.interrupted is True)
-

->
-> Open a public LangSmith run for this example.
-
-**Multi-turn**
-
-Each invocation starts with a fresh subagent state. The subagent does not remember previous calls:
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
-
-# First call
-response = agent.invoke(
-    {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me about apples"}]},
-    config=config,
-)
-# Subagent message count: 4
-
-# Second call - subagent starts fresh, no memory of apples
-response = agent.invoke(
-    {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Now tell me about bananas"}]},
-    config=config,
-)
-# Subagent message count: 4 (still fresh!)
-```
-
-**Multiple subgraph calls**
-
-Multiple calls to the same subgraph work without conflicts, since each invocation gets its own checkpoint namespace:
-
-```python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}
-config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
-
-# LLM calls ask_fruit_expert for both apples and bananas
-response = agent.invoke(
-    {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me about apples and bananas"}]},
-    config=config,
-)
-# Subagent message count: 4 (apples - fresh)
-# Subagent message count: 4 (bananas - fresh)
-```
+> [tab] Interrupts
+>
+> Each invocation can use `interrupt()` to pause and resume. Add `interrupt()` to a tool function to require user approval before proceeding:

+> ```
